title: Protocol for Screening Facultative Parthenogenesis in Drosophila
author: Sperling, Glover

steps.title: Establish baseline parthenogenesis levels
steps.instruction: Screen multiple Drosophila species and strains to determine the natural frequency of parthenogenesis. Test approximately 500 virgin females to detect low‑level parthenogenesis (≥1 offspring per 500 females) and test as few as 30 virgin females to detect high‑level parthenogenesis (≈3 offspring per female). Include at least three strains (e.g., w‑, Oregon‑R, and a wild‑caught strain) to assess strain‑specific effects and use the observed rates as a baseline for later genotype testing.

steps.title: Optimize assay temperature
steps.instruction: Perform pilot parthenogenesis assays at 18 °C, 25 °C, and 29 °C using the bam RNAi line (the first genotype that showed reproducible parthenogenesis). Record that the highest parthenogenesis occurs at 18 °C, moderate levels at 25 °C, and none at 29 °C. Choose 25 °C for subsequent screens because experiments complete in ~3 months at this temperature versus ~5 months at 18 °C. Optionally, after egg laying, keep eggs at a different temperature if desired.

steps.title: Set up negative gene variant controls
steps.instruction: Include the following negative controls to assess background parthenogenesis: (1) an allele for CG3436, (2) two alleles for dhd, (3) an allele and an RNAi line for Klp64D, (4) an allele and an RNAi line for Trx‑2, and (5) an allele and an RNAi line for white (w). Note any low‑level parthenogenesis observed in these controls.

steps.title: Set up genotype background controls
steps.instruction: Because the UAS/Gal4 system is used, include controls for the driver constructs and balancer stocks: bam‑Gal4; maternal tubulin (MTB)‑Gal4 on the 2nd and 3rd chromosomes; nanos (nos)‑Gal4; and the double‑balancer stock employed in the screen. Record that MTB‑Gal4 and nos‑Gal4 each show a small degree of parthenogenesis.

steps.title: Prepare and maintain fly stocks
steps.instruction: Expand or amplify the chosen stock/strain/species before the assay to obtain enough virgin females. Prepare ample fly food for large‑scale collection and maintain the flies with weekly care throughout the experiment. Remember that some Drosophila species may live 5–6 months at 25 °C.
